summary: LLM token prices fell roughly 80% between 2025 and 2026, yet enterprise API spend passed $8.4 billion in 2025 and is on track to double again — the defining paradox of 2026 AI economics is that falling prices coexist with exploding bills as usage scales. Inference-time optimization attacks this directly: combining prompt caching, model routing, compression, output control, and semantic caching can realistically cut API spend by 50-80% with no change to output quality. The highest-leverage, lowest-risk lever is prompt caching, which cuts repeated-prefix input costs by up to 90%.

techniques.name: Prompt Caching (provider-native)
techniques.description: Stores the computed key-value tensors behind a repeated static prompt prefix (system prompts, RAG knowledge bases, tool definitions) so the provider does not recompute them on each request. The saving is structural, not a quality trade-off. Order prompts so the static portion stays at the front and truly static.
techniques.savings: 41-90% on cached input tokens (PwC 500-session study: 41-80%, up to 90% on stable prefixes)
techniques.example: A coding assistant with a 10,000-token system prompt shared across all sessions moves the static instructions to the top of the request; Anthropic/OpenAI then cache the prefix and bill cached tokens at ~10-25% of the normal input rate.

techniques.name: Semantic Caching
techniques.description: Caches full responses keyed by the semantic meaning (embedding similarity) of a query rather than exact text match, so paraphrased or near-identical questions return a stored answer without hitting the model at all. Complementary to prompt caching, which reduces per-token cost while semantic caching eliminates entire calls.
techniques.savings: 30-60% depending on query repetition (typical 45% cache hit rate)
techniques.example: A customer support bot embeds each incoming question; when a new query has >0.95 cosine similarity to a cached one ('How do I reset my password?' vs 'password reset steps'), it serves the cached answer and skips the LLM entirely.

techniques.name: Model Routing (frontier-to-budget tiering)
techniques.description: Routes each request to the cheapest model capable of handling it — a lightweight classifier or heuristic sends simple queries to budget-tier models and only escalates hard queries to flagship models. Flagship models cost 4-16x more than budget tiers for identical token counts.
techniques.example: Route 70% of traffic to GPT-4o-mini/GPT-3.5, 25% to a mid-tier model, and 5% to GPT-4o; a 1M-conversation/month chatbot drops from $3,250 (flagship at $2.50/$10.00) to ~$195 on a budget tier at $0.15/$0.60 — a 16x difference.

techniques.name: Prompt Compression
techniques.description: Reduces the number of input tokens by removing redundancy, trimming few-shot examples, summarizing long context, or using compression models (e.g. LLMLingua) that drop low-information tokens while preserving meaning.
techniques.example: Run a 20,000-token RAG context through LLMLingua to compress it to ~12,000 tokens before sending, cutting input cost ~30% with negligible answer-quality loss.

techniques.name: Output Length Control
techniques.description: Caps and constrains generated tokens — the expensive side of the bill, since output tokens cost 4-5x input tokens — using max_tokens limits, 'be concise' instructions, structured/JSON output, and stop sequences.
techniques.example: Set max_tokens=150 and instruct 'answer in one sentence, JSON only' for a classification task, cutting a verbose 400-token response down to ~120 tokens.

techniques.name: Batch Processing
techniques.description: Submits non-urgent requests through provider batch APIs that run asynchronously (within 24h) at a discounted rate, ideal for offline workloads like evals, summarization, and data enrichment.
techniques.example: Submit a nightly job of 100,000 document summaries via the OpenAI Batch API instead of real-time calls, paying half the standard per-token rate.

techniques.name: KV Cache Management (self-hosted inference)
techniques.description: At the inference-server level (vLLM, TGI, SGLang), prefix-sharing and paged KV cache reuse recomputed attention state across requests with shared prefixes, raising throughput and lowering cost per token on self-hosted/open-model deployments.
techniques.savings: Varies; 2-4x throughput gains on shared-prefix workloads
works_with: self-hosted open models (Llama, Mistral, Qwen) via vLLM, SGLang, TGI
techniques.example: Enable vLLM automatic prefix caching so that 1,000 agent requests sharing the same system prompt reuse the cached KV blocks instead of recomputing attention for every call.

techniques.name: Monitoring & Observability
techniques.description: Instrument token usage, cost-per-feature, cache hit rates, and model mix to find waste — you cannot optimize what you cannot see. Monitoring is the fifth lever that makes the other four measurable and tunable.
techniques.savings: Indirect; typically surfaces 10-30% of spend as reducible waste
techniques.example: Pipe all traffic through Helicone and discover one feature is sending unbounded 8k-token contexts, then add a cap that cuts its cost 40%.

tools.name: GPTCache
tools.description: Open-source semantic caching library that stores LLM responses and serves cached answers for semantically similar queries using embeddings and a vector store.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source); you pay only for the backing vector/cache store

tools.name: Redis (LangCache / semantic cache)
tools.description: In-memory data store offering semantic caching for LLMs via vector similarity search, used for exact-match and semantic response caching at low latency.
tools.pricing_paid: Free OSS; Redis Cloud from ~$5/mo, Enterprise custom pricing

tools.name: LiteLLM
tools.description: Unified proxy/SDK for 100+ LLM providers with built-in caching, model routing/fallbacks, budget controls, and spend tracking behind a single OpenAI-compatible API.
tools.pricing_paid: Free OSS; LiteLLM Enterprise from ~$250/mo for SSO, governance, and support

tools.name: Helicone
tools.description: LLM observability and gateway platform providing cost/token monitoring, caching, rate limiting, and request logging via a one-line proxy integration.
tools.pricing_paid: Free tier (10k requests/mo); paid from ~$20/mo, enterprise custom

tools.name: LangChain / LangCache
tools.description: Framework for building LLM apps with built-in caching integrations (in-memory, Redis, SQLite, semantic) plus routing and prompt management utilities.

tools.name: Bifrost
tools.description: High-performance LLM gateway offering semantic caching that pairs with provider-native prompt caching, plus routing and failover to reduce input tokens by an order of magnitude.
tools.pricing_paid: Free OSS core; managed/enterprise pricing on request

tools.name: LLMLingua
tools.description: Microsoft open-source prompt-compression toolkit that uses a small model to drop low-information tokens, compressing prompts up to 20x with minimal quality loss.

tools.name: Langfuse
tools.description: Open-source LLM observability and analytics platform for tracing, token/cost tracking, evals, and prompt management.
tools.pricing_paid: Free OSS/Hobby; cloud from ~$29/mo, enterprise custom

tools.name: vLLM
tools.description: High-throughput open-source inference engine with PagedAttention and automatic prefix (KV) caching for cost-efficient self-hosted serving of open models.
tools.pricing_paid: Free (open source); you pay only for compute

tools.name: OpenRouter
tools.description: Unified API marketplace routing requests across hundreds of models/providers with automatic price and availability-based routing and fallbacks.
tools.pricing_paid: Free to use; pay per-token at provider rates plus small margin

quick_wins: Turn on provider-native prompt caching and reorder prompts so the static system prompt, tool definitions, and RAG context sit at the front — up to 90% off repeated input tokens with zero quality loss.
Set max_tokens limits and add 'be concise / JSON only' instructions to cap the expensive output side of the bill, saving 20-50% on output tokens.
Route the majority of simple queries to a budget-tier model (e.g. GPT-4o-mini) and reserve flagship models for hard cases — a 16x cost difference for identical token counts.
Add a semantic cache (GPTCache or Redis) in front of repetitive, high-volume queries to eliminate entire LLM calls at a ~45% hit rate.
Pipe all traffic through an observability gateway (Helicone, Langfuse, or LiteLLM) to surface which features waste tokens before optimizing anything else.
